RU-EX-01-001.notes: голова (head, body part) is the native East Slavic form with полногласие (оло); глава (head of a state or organisation) is the Church Slavonic form with ла. The Slavonic form is the abstract or elevated one.

RU-EX-01-002.notes: Млечный Путь (Milky Way) keeps the Church Slavonic form; молочный (dairy) is the everyday East Slavic word. The same pair gives млекопитающее (mammal).

RU-EX-01-003.notes: Отче is the old vocative of отец, preserved in prayer: Отче наш (Our Father). Modern Russian has no vocative case for most nouns.

RU-EX-01-004.notes: Господи is the old vocative of Господь. It survives as a common exclamation of surprise or despair. In prayer, it's the address to God.

RU-EX-02-001.notes: The suffix -ну- turns an imperfective into a perfective of a single instance: чихать → чихнуть (sneeze once). These are called semelfactives.

RU-EX-02-002.notes: прыгать → прыгнуть (one jump). The perfective focuses on the single act. The imperfective прыгать covers repeated jumping.

RU-EX-02-003.notes: подмигивать → подмигнуть (wink once). The past -нула keeps the suffix. The imperfective подмигивать also describes repeated winks.

RU-EX-02-004.notes: щас is a casual pronunciation of сейчас, now often written in chats. It's never used in formal writing.

RU-EX-02-005.notes: чё (also чо) is a casual pronunciation of что, common in many regions. It sounds uneducated to some listeners.
RU-EX-02-005.flag: tr: Whatcha doing? is American; changed to British usage

RU-EX-02-006.notes: здрасте is a fast-speech form of здравствуйте. It's polite but casual. In very fast speech, it can shrink further to здрасьте.

RU-EX-02-007.notes: типа (like, sort of) is a filler from the genitive of тип. It's informal and associated with young speakers.

RU-EX-02-008.notes: короче (literally 'shorter') is a filler meaning 'anyway, long story short'. It's very common in speech.

RU-EX-02-009.notes: спс is a texting abbreviation of спасибо, made from its consonants. Likewise пжл (пожалуйста). Other texting abbreviations: плз, ок.

RU-EX-02-010.notes: норм is a clipped form of нормально, common in speech and texts. It means 'fine, OK'. The full form нормально is neutral.

RU-EX-03-001.notes: парадная (building entrance) is the St Petersburg word; Muscovites say подъезд. It's an adjective used as a noun, hence у парадной.

RU-EX-03-002.notes: поребрик (kerb) is the St Petersburg word; elsewhere it's бордюр. The pair is a popular marker of Petersburg speech.

RU-EX-03-003.notes: шаверма is the St Petersburg word for shawarma; Moscow says шаурма. The accusative is шаверму. The difference is a classic Moscow / Petersburg talking point.

RU-EX-03-004.notes: шо is the southern (and Ukrainian-influenced) pronunciation of что. It's perceived as strongly regional.

RU-EX-04-001.notes: Ask the question: что делать? → infinitive with -ться (учиться); что делает? → third person with -тся (учится). The ь follows the infinitive.

RU-EX-04-002.notes: After нравится, the infinitive answers что делать?, so -ться: заниматься. She does it answers что делает?, so -тся.

RU-EX-04-003.notes: ъ is written after a prefix ending in a consonant before е, ё, ю, я: объясню. It keeps the й sound. Without ъ, the word would be read with a soft б.

RU-EX-04-004.notes: съесть (eat up) takes ъ after the prefix с- before е: съел. сел (sat) is a different word. The ъ is also written in съезд and съёмка.

RU-EX-04-005.notes: подъезд has ъ after the prefix под- before е. The genitive is подъезда. The same ъ appears in подъём and подъехать.

RU-EX-04-006.notes: небольшой is written together as a single adjective (fairly small); не большой is written apart when contrasted with а: не большой, а маленький.

RU-EX-04-007.notes: не is always written separately from verbs: не знаю. незнаю is a common error. Exceptions are verbs that don't exist without не (ненавидеть).
RU-EX-04-007.text: Я {{c1::не знаю::незнаю or не знаю?}}, что сказать.
RU-EX-04-007.tr: I don't know what to say.
RU-EX-04-007.flag: dup: replaced Я не знаю (also inside A1-07-013)

RU-EX-04-008.notes: не раз means 'more than once'; ни разу (+ не) means 'not once'. The vowel changes the meaning completely.
RU-EX-04-008.text:
(A man speaking) Я {{c1::не раз::не раз or ни разу?}} был там.
(A man speaking) Я {{c2::ни разу::не раз or ни разу?}} не видел снега.
RU-EX-04-008.tr: I've been there more than once. / I've never once seen snow.
RU-EX-04-008.flag: dup: replaced Я ни разу там не был (near-identical to B1 Он ни разу там не был); text: added (A man speaking)

RU-EX-04-009.notes: не один means 'more than one'; ни один (+ не) means 'not a single one'. The same pattern as не раз / ни разу.

RU-EX-04-010.notes: A participle with не and no dependent words is written together: непрочитанная книга. It functions like an adjective.

RU-EX-04-011.notes: With a dependent word (мной), не is written separately: не прочитанная мной. The participle keeps its verbal force.

RU-EX-04-012.notes: Short participles are always written separately from не: не решён. They behave like verbs. The long participle нерешённый would be written together.

RU-EX-05-001.notes: An adjective from an imperfective verb, without prefix or dependents, has one н: жареная картошка. It describes a quality.

RU-EX-05-002.notes: With a dependent phrase (на масле), the word becomes a participle with нн: жаренная на масле. The meaning is more verbal.

RU-EX-05-003.notes: деревянный is one of three exceptions with -янн- (деревянный, стеклянный, оловянный). Other -ян- adjectives have one н.

RU-EX-05-004.notes: ветреный (windy) has one н, but безветренный has two. It's a known exception. Other examples: обветренный, проветренный.

RU-EX-05-005.notes: кожаный (leather) has one н, from the suffix -ан-. Likewise песчаный, серебряный. The participle кожанный doesn't exist.

RU-EX-05-006.notes: то же (the same thing) is a pronoun + particle, written apart; тоже (also) is one word. Test: add самое: то же самое.

RU-EX-05-007.notes: так же (in the same way) is written apart when followed by как; также (also) is one word. Test: if тоже fits instead, write также.

RU-EX-05-008.notes: что бы ни (whatever) is two words; чтобы (in order to) is one. Test: remove бы and the sentence still works.

RU-EX-05-009.notes: в течение (over the period of) ends in -е. в течении (in the current) is a noun phrase with -и. The same goes for в продолжение (throughout).

RU-EX-05-010.notes: кое- with a preposition is written apart without a hyphen: кое о чём. Without a preposition: кое-что.

RU-EX-05-011.notes: по- + adjective in -ому forms an adverb with a hyphen: по-новому. Likewise по-русски, по-моему. Likewise по-английски, по-моему, по-твоему.

RU-EX-05-012.notes: пол- is hyphenated before a vowel, л or a capital letter: пол-литра, пол-яблока, пол-Москвы. Otherwise it's joined: полчаса.

RU-EX-05-013.notes: Feminine nouns ending in a sibilant take ь: ночь, мышь, речь. Masculine ones don't: нож, врач. The same goes for печь, дочь, ложь.

RU-EX-05-014.notes: Masculine nouns ending in a sibilant have no ь: нож, ключ, плащ. The genitive is ножа, with stress on the ending. Feminine ones take ь: ночь, мышь.

RU-EX-05-015.notes: The ты ending -шь always has ь: читаешь, пишешь. This rule has no exceptions. The same applies to the reflexive: учишься.

RU-EX-05-016.notes: Genitive plurals of feminine nouns ending in a sibilant have no ь: задач, туч, рощ. Likewise туча → туч, роща → рощ.
RU-EX-05-016.text: Нам нужно решить несколько {{c1::задач::tasks · genitive plural (ь or not?)}}.
RU-EX-05-016.tr: We need to solve several problems.
RU-EX-05-016.flag: dup: replaced У меня много задач (near-identical to A2 У меня много друзей)

RU-EX-05-017.notes: Adverbs ending in a sibilant usually take ь (вскачь, настежь), but замуж, невтерпёж and уж are exceptions.

RU-EX-05-018.notes: при- means arrival or nearness: прибывать (arrive). пре- means 'very' or 'over': пребывать (stay, be). The two look alike but mean different things.
RU-EX-05-018.text: Самолёт {{c1::прибывает::arrive (пре- or при-?)}} в Москву в полдень.
RU-EX-05-018.tr: The plane arrives in Moscow at midday.
RU-EX-05-018.flag: dup: replaced Поезд прибывает в пять (near-identical to B1 Поезд уходит в пять)

RU-EX-05-019.notes: пребывать (stay, be present) has пре-. It's an official word: пребывание в Москве. The noun is пребывание.

RU-EX-05-020.notes: Days of the week are written with a lower-case letter: в понедельник. So are months. Only at the start of a sentence would it be capitalised.

RU-EX-05-021.notes: Language and nationality adjectives are written lower-case: русский язык. Only country names are capitalised.

RU-EX-06-001.notes: Сколько времени? is the colloquial way to ask the time. Сколько время? is non-standard. Который час? is the more neutral question.

RU-EX-06-002.notes: Cities take в, so 'from' is из: из Москвы. с Москвы is regional or colloquial. The opposite is в Москву.

RU-EX-06-003.notes: школа takes в, so 'from' is из: из школы. со школы is common in speech but non-standard. The same goes for из университета.

RU-EX-06-004.notes: кофе is masculine in the standard language: мой кофе остыл. Dictionaries accept the neuter only as colloquial. In careful speech, keep it masculine.

RU-EX-06-005.notes: A verbal adverb must share its subject with the main clause: подъезжая, я уронил. Chekhov's mocking example used у меня слетела шляпа.

RU-EX-06-006.notes: With a noun (языке), the phrase is на русском языке; по-русски is the adverb. по-русски языке is impossible.
